title: Finite Kubo-Mori derivative transfer through a shifted energy second moment
question: Does the finite Kubo-Mori spectral second moment admit an explicit shifted-energy transfer bound S(delta_H D) <= 8 Tr(rho K^2)||D||^2 for the actual Q3 histories, and what hypothesis remains for a common-core theorem?

model.transfer_bound: The termwise inequalities give the safe finite-dimensional bound S <= 8 M2 ||D||_HS^2; the sharper S <= 8 M2 ||D||_operator^2 is tested only as an empirical candidate on the declared Q3 rows.
model.interpretation: The finite Hilbert-Schmidt inequality is a conditional bridge; a volume/source/beta-uniform local M2, a common-core D bound, and any operator-norm replacement remain separate hypotheses.

adversarial_review.check: K is shifted by the actual finite spectral minimum plus I, so the transfer inequality uses nonnegative k_i and is invariant under scalar energy shifts.
The finite lanes verify L(p_i,p_j)<= (p_i+p_j)/2 and use the equal-probability diagonal limit.
The aggregate 8 M2 ||D||^2 bound is tested with the actual matrix operator norm; no Hilbert-Schmidt replacement is silently made.
M2 is the global finite Gibbs moment in each row; no local or volume-uniform M2 is inferred from finite data.
The finite matrix inequality does not establish product domains, modular tails, or a common unbounded core.
Direct Cauchy, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks exact rational gap and arithmetic-mean transfer fixtures; the finite matrix norm inequality is independently executed in Python and all common-core/uniform QFT assertions remain open.

qft_interface.closed: A finite conditional bridge from the Kubo-Mori derivative spectral moment to a shifted Gibbs energy second moment, with a proven Hilbert-Schmidt bound and an operator-norm candidate checked on actual rows.
qft_interface.open: A local/source/volume/beta-uniform M2 estimate on an unbounded common core, a general operator-norm replacement, direct D control, modular-domain transfer, product/core density, exhaustion independence, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum and Pre-A.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: The factor 8 Hilbert-Schmidt inequality identifies a sufficient finite analytic interface; the sharper operator-norm statement is empirical here and neither is itself a thermodynamic QFT theorem.

no_overclaim: The finite Hilbert-Schmidt transfer bound is exact within the declared finite spectral setting. The operator-norm version is only a candidate passing these rows. Neither proves a uniform local energy moment, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, common alpha, Sector A, Pre-A, or any Clay statement.
